To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DOI inhibits mPFC neurons and this inhibition is mediated by 2-HT2 receptor activation.
DOI potentiates and inhibits GLU-induced activity and inhibits spontaneous activity of mPFc cells and that this inhibitory action of (+/-)-DOI is mediated by 2-HT2 receptors.
DOI inhibits spontaneous and GLU induced activity of mPFc cells via 5-HT2A/2C receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors in the regulation of the activity of neurons in the medial pre-frontal cortex.
the neuropharmacological characterization of the 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors in the medial prefontal cortex (mPFC).
understanding the neurochemical mechanisms underlying the behavioral effects of the hallucinogen 1-(2-5-dimethox-4-iodo-phenyl)-2-ami-no-propane (DOI) in animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DOI-induced inhibition of mPFc neuronal excitability is mediated by 2 receptor subtype(s).
DOI has an overall inhibitory effect on mPFc neuronal function, and that the inhibitory action of the 5-HT receptor agonist is mediated by 2-HT2 receptors.
5-HT2 agonists, including DOI, are predominantly inhibitory on mPFc neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of (+/-)-DOI in the mPFc can be explained as follows.
5-HT1 receptors are inhibitory and 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 are excitatory.
the inhibitory effect of DOI on mPFc neuronal cells is a direct one, and mediated by 5- HT2 receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DOI inhibits mPFC neuronal activity in a 5-HT2-receptor dependent manner.
DOI inhibits spontaneous and excitatory amino acid-induced activity of cells of mPFc and that the inhibitory action is due to 5-HT2A receptor activation.
DOI is not a good tool to use to probe 5-HT2A receptor-mediated actions in the mPFc.
